title: White House AI Evaluation Framework Completed but Kept Confidential: Companies Can't Even See the Full Text, Open Source Issue Becomes the Focus Again

content_html:
According to sources, the White House is not planning to publicly release its newly developed advanced AI model evaluation framework. This voluntary framework has significant implications for global AI safety, but specific details will only be shared with relevant companies involved in the development process.

This means that companies, policymakers, researchers, and U.S. overseas allies outside of this process will not have an accurate understanding of how the White House will implement its key AI policies. On Tuesday, the White House held a working-level meeting with industry representatives to communicate about the framework, but companies not invited to the meeting remain unaware of the specific content of the framework.

Executive Order First, Security Evaluation Standards Have Been Classified as Confidential

The release of this framework comes amid the AI industry's deepening challenges, including frequent high-risk cyberattacks and the rapid technological advancements by Chinese AI developers. According to an executive order issued in June, this voluntary framework aims to provide AI developers with a mechanism to collaborate with the government to determine whether their models fall under regulatory scope.

The framework is also expected to establish rules allowing the government to access relevant information within up to 30 days before the release of an AI model, covering requirements such as confidentiality, cybersecurity, internal personnel risks, intellectual property, and non-disclosure agreements. The executive order explicitly states that the technical benchmark testing process used to evaluate AI model network capabilities will be classified as confidential, and the order itself does not require the voluntary framework to be made public.

Open Source Issues Rise Again, Huang Renxun Visits Washington

Notably, open-source models were also discussed during this meeting, with representatives from the renowned chip manufacturer NVIDIA attending. Previously, Huang Renxun, CEO of NVIDIA and an advocate for open source, visited Washington last week to meet with U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and the President.

Controversies surrounding Chinese open-source AI models continue to intensify—factions led by OpenAI and Anthropic are trying to push for restrictions on the use of Chinese open-source models, while giants like NVIDIA, Microsoft, and Meta have jointly opposed this. By incorporating open-source issues into the AI evaluation framework discussion, the White House indicates that this debate is rising from the industry level to the policy decision-making level. Both the White House and the EU have refused to comment on the secrecy of the framework, and the UK government has also not responded. When even participating companies are kept in the dark about the regulatory rules that the world's most powerful AI models will face, this "completed but unseen" framework may already reveal much.

content_html_zh:
据消息人士透露，白宫不打算公开发布其新开发的先进人工智能模型评估框架。 这一自愿框架对全球人工智能安全具有重大影响，但具体细节只会与参与开发过程的相关公司共享。

这意味着在此过程之外的公司、政策制定者、研究人员和美国海外盟友将无法准确了解白宫将如何实施其关键的人工智能政策。 周二，白宫与行业代表举行了工作级会议，就该框架进行沟通，但未受邀参加会议的企业仍不了解该框架的具体内容。

行政命令先行，安全评估标准已列为机密

该框架的发布正值人工智能行业面临日益严峻的挑战，包括频繁的高风险网络攻击和中国人工智能开发者的快速技术进步。 根据 6 月份发布的行政命令，这一自愿框架旨在为人工智能开发者提供一种与政府合作的机制，以确定他们的模型是否属于监管范围。

该框架预计还将制定规则，允许政府在人工智能模型发布前最多 30 天内访问相关信息，涵盖保密、网络安全、内部人事风险、知识产权和保密协议等要求。 该行政命令明确指出，用于评估AI模型网络能力的技术基准测试流程将被列为机密，并且命令本身并不要求公开自愿框架。

开源问题再起，黄仁勋访问华盛顿

值得注意的是，本次会议还讨论了开源模型，著名芯片制造商NVIDIA的代表也出席了会议。 此前，开源倡导者、NVIDIA首席执行官黄仁勋上周访问华盛顿，会见美国商务部长霍华德·卢特尼克和总统。

围绕中国开源AI模型的争议不断加剧，以OpenAI和Anthropic为首的派系试图推动限制中国开源模型的使用，而NVIDIA、微软、Meta等巨头则联合反对。 白宫通过将开源问题纳入人工智能评估框架讨论，表明这场争论正在从行业层面上升到政策决策层面。 白宫和欧盟都拒绝就该框架的保密性发表评论，英国政府也没有做出回应。 当即使是参与公司也对世界上最强大的人工智能模型将面临的监管规则一无所知时，这个“完整但看不见”的框架可能已经揭示了很多东西。
